newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia police shoot dead four in crime roundup.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia police shoot dead four in crime roundup.

text.p: Indonesian police shot dead four robbery suspects when they tried to evade arrest during a crackdown on criminals in the West Java city of Bandung, the Kompas newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The report quoted Bandung police chief Colonel Erwin Mappaseng as telling reporters the four men, including a former soldier, were shot in two separate incidents early on Tuesday.
"There is no order to shoot criminals on the spot. These shootings were forced because in the situation there were very limited options," Mappaseng was quoted as saying.
"They continued to run even though warning shots had been fired so that (the police) were forced to shoot in their direction to incapacitate them," he said.

In the early 1980s, Indonesian security forces executed thousands of criminals on the island of Java in a wave of "mysterious killings" which President Suharto later described as necessary "shock therapy" in the face of rising crime rates.
The Kompas report said the Bandung round-up also netted 10 other criminals from five different gangs.
